correctness.rationale: PASS: Fourier aliasing of the periodic Poisson kernel P_r gives exact N-point shifted average P_(r^N)(N Theta); a uniform cell shift makes its argument uniform. Thus mean 1 and Var(A)=2r^(2N)/[m(1-r^(2N))]. In a triangular array q=r^N→1, set epsilon=1-q and L=m epsilon. At L→0, absent hits within epsilon-scaled angular core (probability O(mKepsilon)), while outer-arc expectation is asymptotically 1-2 arctan(K)/pi; then K→∞ and Markov prove A→0 in probability despite unbiasedness. At L→lambda∈(0,∞), scaling u=epsilon x and domination by 1/(1+x²) in the exact Laplace transform yields the Poisson shot noise of intensity lambda/(2pi) with mark 2/[lambda(1+x²)]; Campbell formulas give mean 1, variance 1/lambda. At L→∞, exact variance gives L² consistency and maximum normalized triangular summand O(1/sqrt(L)), hence Lindeberg CLT sqrt(L)(A-1)⇒N(0,1). The three subsequential cases prove iff L→∞ for convergence in probability/mean square; q→1 also implies epsilon~N(1-r). Independently verified Fourier aliasing numerically at 36 parameter values. Finite comparisons do not replace the weak-convergence proof.
